hints: Factor out $\sin\theta$ to obtain $\sin\theta(4\cos\theta + 1) = 0$, giving two cases: $\sin\theta = 0$ or $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$.
Determine the solutions for $\theta$ within the open interval $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$, noting that $\theta = 0^\circ$ and $\theta = 180^\circ$ are excluded by the strict inequality.
walkthrough:
Factor out $\sin\theta$ and combine over a common denominator:
$$\sin\theta\left(4 + \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{\sin\theta(4\cos\theta + 1)}{\cos\theta} = 0$$

Set each factor to zero to obtain two separate trigonometric equations:
$$\sin\theta = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad 4\cos\theta + 1 = 0 \implies \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$$

Find solutions in the range $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\sin\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0^\circ, 180^\circ \quad (\text{both excluded by strict interval } 0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ)$$
$$\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4} \implies \theta = 180^\circ - \cos^{-1}(0.25) = 180^\circ - 75.52^\circ \approx 104.5^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Substitutes $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and factors out $\sin\theta$ to get $\sin\theta(4\cos\theta+1)=0$.
ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Identifies $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$ and solves to give $\theta = 104.5^\circ$ within $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$.
